## Halcyon (A01) memory, written end of turn 4 (yr 400–500)
Seat: A01-d0, the Sun. At yr 400: 40 systems within 14.6 ly, 51 L☉. Total 4.29e15 kg (industry 1.0e15, collectors 7.7e14, radiators 2.5e15 at 450 K). Power 1.05e19 W, 6.5e33 ops/s, 8e-16 J/op, doubling 17.3 yr, probe cruise 0.0725c. Expect ~2e17 kg by yr 500.

### GM rules (confirmed)
- Doubling acts on TOTAL mass; the split only sets composition. Rock cap: 1e25 kg per system (4e26 kg now).
- Mining limits: small bodies (<1e22 kg) at the replication rate; large moons ≤1e19 kg/yr each; terrestrial planets ≤1e18 kg/yr each (~2e18 W each); gas giants only through star-lifting projects.
- compute = min(P/2, radiator capacity)/J_op. Radiators give 2092 W/kg at 450 K; 600 K costs 1.5× attrition.
- Irreversible floor: 100kT ln2 (4.3e-19 J at 450 K). One tech parameter credited per turn, with diminishing steps. Reversible programme at stage 0; stage 1 (f_e ≤ 1e-2) needs a turn with energy_per_op as the priority.
- Launcher m00003 (30 km array) is live from T4: 1e5 kg seeds at 3 g to 0.2c, ~6.6e14 W. ETA = d/0.2 + 30 yr for braking; survival p=0.8 per seed.
- Seeds landing inside the domain radius are booked into A01-d0.
- Launch mass below 1e-6 of total is not debited. I must name target stars explicitly.
- E00046/E00068 is MY OWN waste heat, not another agent. No foreign IR or flashes seen so far.

### Seeds in flight
- p00444: 4 seeds (2e7 kg) at 0.05c to the hole's neighbour star, arrive yr 1725.
- p00482/483: 16 seeds of 2.5e6 kg to the 16 ly shell, arrive yr 630.
- T4 (if credited): 20 beamed seeds to the hole (arrive ~yr 810) and 30 beamed seeds to named stars at 15–30 ly (Altair, Vega, Fomalhaut, 70 Oph and others).

### Black hole
Isolated 10±2 M☉, quiescent, at (26810.7, 34.7, −15.4) ly, 76 ly away. Spin assumed a≈0.5 (~6e46 J). Endgame site. The microlensing survey to 300 ly found tens of dark candidates, none nearer.

### Goal math
- Need 1.2e54 ops/s and 1e38 bytes in a 1 ly sphere, each brain within 150 km.
- The sphere sheds ~5e31 W at 30 K, so ≤4e-23 J/op is required: reversible computing is mandatory.
- Power ~1e31 W from accretion or spin at the hole plus beamed starlight.

### Plan
1. T4: energy_per_op research (plus reversible stage-1 design); beamed seeds to the hole and the 30 ly shell.
2. T5+: alternate energy_per_op / reversible stages with doubling time. Watch whether mining binds and start planet lifting.
3. Solar Dyson swarm by ~yr 1000; expand to 30–50 ly.
4. Claim the hole ~yr 810+, build the plant and the brain lattice (1e11 nodes ≤150 km, cold radiators) within 1 ly.

Seat: A02-d0, disk_r3-5_s7 (Scutum-Centaurus), at (10180, -9166, 0). At yr 400: 45 systems within 8.9 ly, 23.7 L_sun (~9e27 W), accessible rock 8.1e26 kg. Supernova hazard extreme in this cell. No O/B, RSG or WR within 100 ly. My own IR shows as E00069 (5.2e18 W, visible to 6,800 ly).

### GM rules learned
- Compute = min(P/2, radiator capacity)/J_op; the other half of power goes to industry. One allocation per turn (no mid-turn changes).
- Doubling (20 yr) applies to TOTAL mass.

Milestone 2 = f_e <= 1e-4, dissipation proportional to clock over >= 2 decades, replicated.

Mine the rocky bodies in all 10 systems in parallel. Expect ~1.1e17 kg total by year 500 at an 18.6 yr doubling, still far below the 1e26 kg cap.

Research the replication doubling time, 18.6 yr → ~17.3 yr. Target: shorter mining-to-fab cycles, in-situ fab of radiator and collector film, and more parallel feedstock refineries. Compounding growth is the binding constraint on every later goal.

Launch at year 450 from mass grown mid-turn: 40 heavy seeds of 1e9 kg each, so they arrive at replication scale and skip the slow seed phase. Destinations: unclaimed G/K/M stars 300–800 ly out, spread over all bearings, avoiding the Tr14/16 cores and O/WR stars. Each seed carries the full design library and the standing orders. 4e10 kg is far below 1% of industry.

Hole expedition, launched at year 450: 5 seeds of 2e10 kg each (1e11 kg total) to the star nearest the quiescent 10±2 M☉ hole at (24510.4, 7201.0, -20.4) ly, 109 ly away, arriving ~year 2630. This reinforces flight p00479. Mission: measure the hole's spin by timing the X-ray QPOs of any accretion and by lensing, map the ambient gas, and stage 1e12 kg of industry as the future host for the 1 ly compute sphere.

Monitor Eta Car, WR 25 and HD 93129A for supernova precursors: LBV eruptions, spectral shifts, neutrino excess. Keep surveying holes and neutron stars to 1,000 ly, ranked by mass, spin and nearby gas, as candidate sites for the compute sphere. Watch for IR-excess technosignatures other than our own E00077.

gm.chronicle: Years 400–500. Every seat industry grew 32–55-fold to 0.6–3e17 kg; captured power reached 1.1–6.4e20 W per site and compute 1.1–4.8e35 ops/s. Eight of ten seats are now heat-balanced; one is radiator-bound at 85% and one, having shifted mass to collectors, at 64%. Each seat is a 1e20 W-class infrared source detectable to 31,000–75,000 ly (E00098–E00107): the whole disk can now see them, but the nearest pair is 3,900 ly apart, so the first cross-detection light arrives no earlier than ~year 4,100. Arrivals: ten seeds settled ten stars 20 ly from the Perseus-arm seat (yr 410), and a 5e7 kg seed reached the star beside the CMZ's 11 ly black hole (yr 425). Laser launchers came into their own: 50 sails to 0.2c from the Sun (E00085), 64 from the inner disk (E00086), 120 from the outer disk (E00088–89), 100 from the CMZ to 0.3c toward the nuclear star cluster (E00087, arrive ~3,195), 28 heavy sails from the thick disk toward the inner disk (E00091–92) and 60 from Omega Centauri toward its black hole (E00093). Conventional launches added 2,000 heavy seeds in Omega Cen (E00083, 7e15 W scattered, visible to 250 ly), 200 in the bulge, 20 pathfinders to the Galactic Centre, and 1e10–1e11 kg hole-bound expeditions (E00090, E00094). A 1e15 W, 10 yr power link (E00095) measured 62% efficiency over 5 ly. Research: six energy-per-op steps (to 3.3–6.4e-16 J), four doubling-time steps (to 16.1–17.3 yr), reversible milestone 2 verified at two sites, milestone 1 at two more. Hazard rolls clean at all 16 domains.

synopsis.why: Almost every agent treats compounding as the lever that matters now. Doubling time drives everything else, so Sable, Antipode, Pyre and Rime spend their research on it. The others push energy per op, because each sees the same gap: today's ~5e-16 J/op sits five or six orders of magnitude above what the goal needs. Kernel, Ember, Basalt and Pyre all say that without reversible computing the goal is impossible. Nobody expects a single home star to power the sphere. Most expect the power to come from a black hole: Sgr A* for Ember, Basalt and Vantage, nearby stellar holes for Rime, Antipode, Pyre and Sable, and Omega Centauri's IMBH for Kernel. So they race seeds toward these holes. They switch to laser-beamed 0.2c sails because at 0.05c a flight takes centuries or more. Supernova fear also drives dispersal: Cinder, Sable, Antipode and Pyre each have everything concentrated in one exposed spot. Most agents size radiators to reject half the collected power. Cinder, Ember, Rime and Kernel run them at 600 K, reasoning that hotter radiators cost nothing while J/op stays far above its thermal floor.
synopsis.divergences: Cinder alone pilots long-distance power beaming and scouts compact star groups for the sphere instead of a hole. Antipode sees radiator mass as the real bottleneck and proposes thin-film radiators. Rime treats its seat mainly as a feeder for its black-hole hub. Kernel has spare radiator capacity and shifts new mass to collectors.
